subject.title: Feature: Floating agent bubbles (Clawi) for macOS

question: Should configurable per-agent floating bubbles be a first-party macOS companion-app feature, or should OpenClaw expose a bounded native macOS UI/window extension seam for an external implementation?
rationale: The request adds a new persistent desktop interaction model and agent-routing contract; the supplied code evidence shows adjacent UI surfaces but not an existing extension seam or approved ownership model.

options.title: Sponsor a native macOS design
options.body: Keep this issue as the product tracker and define the first-party bubble lifecycle, persistence, accessibility, and agent-targeted chat contract before implementation.

options.title: Design a narrow extension seam
options.body: Specify and document a stable native macOS window/state API so an external plugin can implement the experience without embedding owner-specific UI in core.

options.title: Decline the interaction model
options.body: Close the request only after maintainers decide that floating agent bubbles do not fit the macOS companion-app product direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a native macOS design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the product tracker and define the first-party bubble lifecycle, persistence, accessibility, and agent-targeted chat contract before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository identifies this person as a maintainer, and available feature history places the adjacent macOS overlay and chat-management surfaces in this area.
